name: read-side-ladder
purpose: Test the premise the whole interface rests on: that the cheap model is bound by expression, not comprehension. The control arm sees 359,701 characters of workbook per task and refuses nothing; LibreCalc as shipped shows 74,459 and refuses one call in five. Four arms on the same 15 tasks and the same model separate the two candidate causes -- how much the model may see, and whether our summary is worse than raw truth.

arms.A_control: bash + view_xlsx + openpyxl, official prompt, 50 calls. MEASURED: 3/15, mod 0.7801, 359,701 chars.
arms.B_shipped: formula-patterns-v1 + formula-blocks-v1, 96-cell ceiling, budget as configured.
arms.C_unbounded: B with --unbounded-reads: no ceiling, no read budget. Isolates VOLUME.
arms.D_raw: grid-v1 + --unbounded-reads: manifest inspect, raw matrices, no limits. Isolates ABSTRACTION.

reads.C much better than B: volume was the constraint; the model is comprehension-bound and the ceiling caused it.
reads.D much better than C: the semantic summary itself misleads; raw truth beats our abstraction.
reads.C approx D approx B: neither. The read side is not the lever and the interface is not what is costing us.

discipline: n=3 per arm. This model swings between exact and 0.9854 on repeat runs of one task, measured at n=4, so no single run of any arm may be quoted. The target is arm A's 3/15 and mod 0.7801; matching it is the bar, exceeding it is the claim.
